script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JANE (30s, nervous but determined) sits across from PETER (40s, successful but unhappy). They sip their coffee in silence.

JANE
(looking at Peter)
I quit my job yesterday. I'm making a change.

PETER
(surprised)
Wow. What's the plan?

JANE
I want to start my own business. A catering company.

PETER
(skeptical)
Catering? Are you sure you have what it takes?

JANE
(smiling)
I've been cooking for friends and family for years. They all say I have a gift.

PETER
(laughs)
Well, that's a start. But there's a lot more to running a business than just cooking.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits at her kitchen table, surrounded by recipe books and business plan templates. Her phone rings.

JANE
(answering)
Hello?

DAVID (friend, 30s)
Hey Jane, how's the new venture going?

JANE
(excited)
Great! I've been researching and planning non-stop.

DAVID
Sounds amazing. I'll help you any way I can.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane meets with SARAH (20s, ambitious), a social media marketing expert. They discuss strategies for promoting Jane's catering business online.

SARAH
We can start with a website, social media accounts, and email marketing.

JANE
(nodding)
Yes, I've got a domain name already. What should I do next?

SARAH
Set up your website and get your social media accounts started. I can help you with content and design.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - EVENING

Jane spends hours designing her website, researching competitors, and setting up her social media accounts. She takes a break to cook dinner for her roommate.

ROOMMATE
(tasting a bite)
This is delicious, Jane. You're going to be a success.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane meets with TOM (50s, experienced business consultant). They discuss the logistics of starting her catering business, such as licenses, insurance, and equipment.

TOM
(pointing to a list)
You'll need a commercial kitchen, licenses, insurance, and equipment.

JANE
(making notes)
Got it. Anything else?

TOM
You'll also need to register your business, create a business plan, and develop a marketing strategy.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane spends nights and weekends working on her business plan, researching equipment, and networking with other caterers. She also starts a blog to share her recipes and catering tips.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane meets with RACHEL (30s, friendly), a local event planner. They discuss potential catering opportunities for Jane's business.

RACHEL
I have a few events coming up that I think would be perfect for your catering services.

JANE
(excited)
Really? That would be amazing!

RACHEL
Yes, but you'll need to provide samples of your food first.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - EVENING

Jane prepares sample dishes for Rachel, who stops by to taste them. Rachel is impressed and promises to book Jane for the upcoming events.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane meets with SARAH again to discuss her social media marketing strategy. They plan content and design for Jane's website and social media channels.

SARAH
We'll start with a pre-launch campaign, then gradually build up to weekly content once your business is up and running.

JANE
(smiling)
I can't wait to see it all come together.

INT. COMMERCIAL KITCHEN - DAY

Jane tours a commercial kitchen space, looking for a place to rent for her catering business. She meets with the owner, MIKE (40s, friendly), who offers her a good deal on a small kitchen.

MIKE
(handing her a lease)
Sign here, and we'll get started right away.

JANE
(excitedly)
I'll sign it now!

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane spends nights and weekends finalizing her business plan, setting up her website, and purchasing equipment. She also continues to network and attend industry events.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane meets with PETER one last time to discuss her progress. He's impressed with her determination and hard work.

PETER
(smiling)
You've really done it, Jane. I'm proud of you.

JANE
(gratefully)
Thank you, Peter. It wouldn't have been possible without your encouragement.

FADE OUT.
